title: A better error message did nothing
body: One case (14 messy category spellings) failed every run: the agent hit the step limit with 30 tool errors. Making the error list the exact values to copy changed nothing. The traces showed the real cause: the tool took an object with free-form keys, and the model could not write keys containing spaces or dots (it sent prem_econ, Bus_, then Bus_z, Bus_g). Switching the tool to a list of {from, to} pairs took the case from 0/3 to 3/3.

title: A pass does not prove the model saw the trap
body: With neutral tool descriptions (no warnings about traps), one case got clearly worse: mixed units went from 3/3 to 1/3. The model guessed what a decimal setting meant, turned 12,500 kg into 12.5, and could not recover because the conversion destroyed the original text. Fixes: parameter-level documentation, an undo tool, and a rule to undo when a result looks wrong.

title: Refuse, or proceed and disclose?
body: When every date could be day-first or month-first, the model picked day-first, converted the column and said so, instead of stopping to ask. A clearer prompt rule did not change that (still 0/3 on two models). The check now lives in the date tool itself: it refuses unless the user stated the order or a value proves it. Offline tests pass; the live re-run is pending because the free API tier ran out of its daily cap.

title: A garbled tool call, then a run that just stopped
body: On real data where missing is written as backslash-N, a dash, N/A or an empty string, one run produced a tool call with its own reasoning leaked into the JSON arguments, then returned no tool call at all and ended unfinished. Fixes: an empty or malformed reply now gets a reminder and a retry, and replace_values gained include_blank so empty strings no longer have to be written inside JSON.
